chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Young drummers: Butch Miles, a young drummer with Woody, Bunky Green's group
summary: Saunders and DeMichael praise young drummers and Bunky Green's youthful band, saying they develop by listening to masters.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Man, I -- right, right, right. I looked at that little young drummer with Woody -- was it Woody?
Not Basie, no. I know Butch, Butch Miles. I mean, --
I think he came through that college.
Did he? I'm not sure about him, but Woody had this little young drummer, man, and he was really saying something. Little bitty there looked like a -- I could spank him.

Oh, yeah, they're really coming on and, see, they listen. They listen, and this is the only way you can really get a true picture of what's happening, is to be able to listen and to -- to the masters and improve themselves, see, and you listen to a improvement product, and this is how they develop.
It really is amazing. You mentioned Bunky Green. Bunky's using a group of youngsters that were either his students or --
-- right out of school. Got a piano player, John Campbell, who really is something. Not many people know him. A young white kid. Looks like he's about 18 or something.
That's what I say. Some of them look so young.
